boundary.definition: The portable format is the versioned composition of independently owned semantic objects, containers, records, schemas, manifests, and content-root protocols.

authorities.identityDomain: logical Fact ids, immutable version roots, Cut roots, and ref transition ids
authorities.versionAxis: Fact record schema and Cut protocol

authorities.identityDomain: canonical root of one exact typed Fact record
Episode identity, sealed content identity, causal closure, and capability set
ordered Episode-owned manifest claims and their sealed root
accepted import manifests, entry deltas, export receipts, and channel cursors
one transfer inventory and its separately rooted entries document
binary page and frame header layout
workspace-relative storage role, not semantic object identity
schema-owned payload bytes and named logical root protocols
authorities.versionAxis: payload schema owner and protocol-selected encoding

authorities.identityDomain: one generated bundle inventory; never runtime semantic authority
authorities.versionAxis: manifest_version, spec_version, and package.version remain independent

authorities.identityDomain: canonical KFX package, facet, capability declaration, and inert Product System metadata
digest of one exact byte string

Episode Manifest.meaning: Typed append-only POD records in an Episode manifest journal; JSON is a folded edge projection.

import/export manifest.meaning: Journal-admitted transfer inventory and receipts, with kungfu.storage.import-manifest/v1 as the JSON edge envelope.

Spec Bundle Manifest.meaning: Generated package pickup and routing inventory for @kungfu-tech/spec; it does not own component semantics.

package JSON Schema.meaning: Identity-neutral KFX declaration of facets, least required capabilities, and inert Product System metadata; it is not runtime authorization.

payload schema.meaning: Exactly one Hana POD owner or one FlatBuffers schema owner interprets a structured payload.

POD layout.meaning: Compiled closed-set record layout guarded by schema_version and compile-time fingerprints.

BFBS.meaning: Exact FlatBuffers reflection schema artifact for an open-layer payload; it is not by itself a logical semantic root.

versionAxes.changesWhen: authority membership, precedence, or domain ownership changes
workspace path or persistence classification changes incompatibly
page_header or frame_header binary layout changes
a typed record layout or interpretation changes
canonical preimage, framing, or algorithm changes
the generated bundle envelope shape changes

compatibility.rule: Compatibility is decided per authority and then composed against an explicit reader profile; no highest, latest, or package version may stand in for all axes.
replacementCriteria: every replaced protocol id has an explicit compatibility owner
required-reader and migration behavior is executable
cross-version vectors prove both retained and refused paths
generated spec and site projections derive from the successor contract

requiredReader.rule: Unknown well-formed bytes may be preserved or inspected under a bounded profile, but canonical fold, admission, and execution require complete compatible semantics.

migrationProtocol.rule: Compatibility is evaluated per protocol axis; supported cold-path edges create receipt-bound successor identities, while downgrade and unsupported edges fail before authority changes.

retainedConformanceCorpus.rule: Released real-byte vectors are content-rooted and append-only; native and independent readers must reproduce the declared outcomes without rewriting retained bytes.

projections.rule: A projection may route, render, or package the authority graph but may not redefine protocol identity, compatibility, or failure semantics.

nonClaims: This contract does not declare the standalone format stable.
This contract does not implement automatic migration or repair.
This contract does not make historical Spec 0.1 normative.
This contract does not make JSON the universal authority encoding.
The retained corpus does not contain private or real user workspace material.
